Mesillat Yesharim 6:1:
An Explanation of the Trait of Alacrity (Zerizut)
After watchfulness comes alacrity, for watchfulness revolves around the "do not do," while alacrity revolves around the "do" — that is (Psalms 34:15): "Turn from evil and do good."
Mesillat Yesharim 6:2: And the matter of alacrity is clear: it is the readiness for the commandments and for completing them fully. In this vein our Sages, of blessed memory, said (Pesachim 4a): "The alacritous perform the commandments at the earliest opportunity."
Mesillat Yesharim 6:3: This is because just as great alertness and much reflection are needed to escape the snares of the inclination and to be delivered from evil, so that it does not rule over us and mix itself into our deeds, so too great alertness and reflection are needed to grasp hold of the commandments and merit them, so that they are not lost to us.
Mesillat Yesharim 6:4: For just as the evil inclination goes about with its stratagems, striving to trap a person in the nets of sin, so it strives to prevent him from performing the commandments and to make them lost to him.
Mesillat Yesharim 6:5: And if he grows lax and lazy and does not strengthen himself to pursue them and hold fast to them, he will certainly remain empty and void of them.
Mesillat Yesharim 6:6: And you will see that man's nature is very heavy, for the earthiness of materiality is coarse; therefore a person does not desire toil and labor. And whoever wishes to merit the service of the Creator, blessed be He, must overcome his own nature and strengthen and hasten himself.
Mesillat Yesharim 6:7: For if he leaves himself in the grip of his own heaviness, he will certainly not succeed. This is what the Tanna said (Avot 5:20): "Be bold as a leopard, light as an eagle, swift as a deer, and mighty as a lion, to do the will of your Father in Heaven." And so the Sages, of blessed memory, counted (Berachot 32b) among the things that require strengthening, Torah and good deeds. And Scripture says explicitly (Joshua 1:7): "Be strong and very courageous, to observe and to do according to all the Torah which Moses My servant commanded you" — for great strengthening is needed for one who wishes to force his nature into its opposite.
Mesillat Yesharim 6:8: And Solomon repeated his warning about this many times, seeing the evil of laziness and the great loss that follows from it, and he said (Proverbs 6:10-11): "A little sleep, a little slumber, a little folding of the hands to lie down; and your poverty comes as a traveler, and your want as an armed man." For the lazy man, even though he does no evil by way of active deed, brings evil upon himself by way of passive omission.
Mesillat Yesharim 6:9: And he said (ibid. 18:9): "One who is slack in his work is also brother to a destroyer." For even though he is not the destroyer who causes evil with his own hands, do not think that he is far from him — rather, he is his brother, and a member of his generation.
Mesillat Yesharim 6:10: And he further explained the evil of the lazy man with a vivid depiction of what befalls and occurs before our very eyes day by day (ibid. 24:30-34): "I passed by the field of a lazy man, and by the vineyard of a man lacking sense, and behold, it was all grown over with thorns; nettles had covered its surface, etc. Then I looked and set my heart upon it; I saw it and received instruction: a little sleep, a little slumber, etc.; so your poverty comes as a traveler, etc."
Mesillat Yesharim 6:11: Now, beyond its plain meaning, which is true as it sounds — namely, what actually happens to the lazy man's field — the Sages, of blessed memory, expounded upon it a fine midrashic teaching, in these words (Yalkut):
Mesillat Yesharim 6:12: "And behold, it was all grown over with thorns" — this refers to one who seeks the meaning of a passage and does not find it.
Mesillat Yesharim 6:13: "It had covered its face, etc." — because he did not labor over them, he sits and declares the pure impure and the impure pure, and breaks down the fences of the Torah scholars. What is his punishment? Solomon explained it (Ecclesiastes 10:8): "And whoever breaks down a fence, a serpent shall bite him."
Mesillat Yesharim 6:14: That is, the evil of the lazy man does not come all at once, but little by little, without his knowing or feeling it — for he is drawn from one evil to another, until he finds himself sunk in the very depths of evil.
Mesillat Yesharim 6:15: At first he merely lacks the effort that was proper for him, and from this it follows that he does not study Torah to the full extent required; and because of this deficiency in study, when he later comes to study, his understanding will be lacking.
Mesillat Yesharim 6:16: And even if his evil ended there, it would already be great. But it goes on increasing further: for when he nevertheless wishes to somehow settle the meaning of that passage or chapter, he will interpret it incorrectly, corrupting the truth and inverting it, transgressing the enactments and breaking down the fences,
Mesillat Yesharim 6:17: and his end is destruction, as is the law for anyone who breaks down a fence. Solomon said: "Then I looked and set my heart upon it" — I reflected upon this matter and saw the great evil within it, which is like a venom that gradually spreads, little by little, whose action is not noticeable until death. This is: "a little sleep, etc.; so your poverty comes as a traveler, and your want as an armed man."
Mesillat Yesharim 6:18: And we see with our own eyes, time and time again, that a person's heart already knows its obligation, and it has already become clear to him what is proper for the salvation of his soul and what is required of him by his Creator — and nevertheless he abandons it, not from any lack of recognition of that obligation, and not for any other reason, but simply because the heaviness of laziness overpowers him.
Mesillat Yesharim 6:19: And he says: I will eat a little, or I will sleep a little, or it is hard for me to leave my house, I have taken off my shirt, how can I put it back on, the heat in the world is fierce, the cold is severe, or it is raining — and all the other excuses and pretexts that fill the mouths of the lazy. And meanwhile, the Torah lies neglected, the service is left undone, and the person abandons his Creator. This is what Solomon says (Ecclesiastes 10:18): "By slothfulness the ceiling sinks in, and through idleness of the hands the house leaks."
Mesillat Yesharim 6:20: And yet if you ask the lazy man himself, he will bring you many sayings from the words of the Sages, verses from Scripture, and arguments of reason — all of which, according to his distorted understanding, direct him to go easy on himself and leave him in the restfulness of his laziness.
Mesillat Yesharim 6:21: And he does not see that these arguments and reasons are not born of his own considered judgment, but flow instead from the source of his laziness; for when laziness gains the upper hand within him, it tilts his mind and reason toward these arguments, so that he will not listen to the voice of the wise and men of sound understanding. This is what Solomon cries out and says (Proverbs 26:16): "The lazy man is wiser in his own eyes than seven men who can answer sensibly."
Mesillat Yesharim 6:22: For laziness does not even let him pay attention to the words of those who reprove him; rather, he considers everyone else misguided fools, and himself alone wise.
Mesillat Yesharim 6:23: And know that this is a great, tried and tested principle in the practice of abstinence: that every leniency requires examination. For even though it may be genuinely correct and proper, it is nonetheless likely to be one of the counsels and deceptions of the inclination; therefore it must be examined through much inquiry and investigation. If, after all this, it proves to be justified, then it is certainly good.
Mesillat Yesharim 6:24: In sum: a person needs great strengthening, to fortify and to overcome himself with alacrity in performing the commandments, casting off from himself the heaviness of laziness that holds him back.
Mesillat Yesharim 6:25: And you will see that the angels are praised for this very good trait, as it is said of them (Psalms 103:20): "mighty in strength, doing His word, hearkening to the voice of His word." And it says (Ezekiel 1:14): "And the living creatures ran and returned, like the appearance of a flash of lightning." Now, man is man and not an angel, so it is impossible for him to attain the might of the angel; but certainly, whatever he can do to draw near to the angel's level, he should do so. And King David used to praise his own portion, saying (Psalms 119:60): "I hastened, and delayed not, to keep Your commandments."
Mesillat Yesharim 7:1:
An Explanation of the Components of Alacrity
The components of alacrity are two: one before the deed, and one after it.
Mesillat Yesharim 7:2: Before the beginning of the deed, it means that a person should not let a commandment go stale,
Mesillat Yesharim 7:3: but rather, when its time arrives, or when it presents itself before him, or when it comes to his mind, he should hasten and rush to seize it and perform it, not allowing time to pass between, lest it grow. For there is no danger like this danger — for in every moment that passes, some new hindrance to the good deed could arise.
Mesillat Yesharim 7:4: And our Sages, of blessed memory, alerted us to the truth of this matter (Bereishit Rabbah 76) concerning the coronation of Solomon, where David said to Benaiah (I Kings 1:33): "and bring him down to Gihon," and Benaiah answered: "Amen; so may the Lord say."
Mesillat Yesharim 7:5: They said, in these words (Bereishit Rabbah 76): Rabbi Pinchas in the name of Rabbi Chanan of Tzippori: But had it not already been said (I Chronicles 22:9), "Behold, a son shall be born to you, he shall be a man of rest"? Rather, many accusers could arise between now and reaching Gihon.
Mesillat Yesharim 7:6: Therefore our Sages, of blessed memory, warned (Mechilta, Exodus 12:17): "And you shall observe the matzot" — a commandment that comes to your hand, do not let it grow stale,
Mesillat Yesharim 7:7: and they said (Nazir 23b): a person should always be first with a matter of a commandment; for because the elder daughter was first with her plan, she merited to precede the younger by four generations in reaching royalty in Israel.
Mesillat Yesharim 7:8: And they said (Pesachim 4a): "The alacritous perform the commandments at the earliest opportunity." And likewise they said (Berachot 6b): "A person should always run for a matter of a commandment, even on the Sabbath."
Mesillat Yesharim 7:9: And in the Midrash they said (Vayikra Rabbah 48): "He will guide us until death" (Psalms 48:15) — with alacrity, like these young maidens, as you say (Psalms 68:26): "in the midst of the maidens playing timbrels."
Mesillat Yesharim 7:10: For alacrity is a trait of great perfection, from which a person's own nature now holds him back. And whoever, at present, overcomes it and grasps hold of it as much as he can — in the future to come he will truly merit it, for the Creator, blessed be He, will grant it to him as his reward in place of the effort he made to pursue it during the time of his service.
Mesillat Yesharim 7:11: But alacrity after the beginning of the deed means that once he has taken hold of a commandment, he should hasten to complete it and not go easy on himself, like one who longs to cast off his burden; rather, he should do so out of fear lest he fail to merit finishing it.
Mesillat Yesharim 7:12: And concerning this our Sages, of blessed memory, warned repeatedly, saying (Bereishit Rabbah 85): whoever begins a commandment and does not complete it — he buries his wife and children.
Mesillat Yesharim 7:13: And they said (ibid.): a commandment is called only by the name of the one who completes it.
Mesillat Yesharim 7:14: And King Solomon, peace be upon him, said (Proverbs 22:29): "Do you see a man diligent in his work? He shall stand before kings; he shall not stand before obscure men."
Mesillat Yesharim 7:15: And the Sages, of blessed memory (Sanhedrin 104a), attributed this praise to him because he hastened in the work of building the Temple and was not lazy about it, delaying it. And likewise they expounded it concerning Moses, peace be upon him, because he hastened in the work of the Tabernacle.
